cleanIntro: The 995TS is the 9mm carbine in Hi-Point's TS line, and it strips further than most owners expect: shroud off, firing assembly out of the stock, breech bolt off the fixed barrel. Two things separate it from its bookmates. It shares a 16-1/2 inch barrel and a counterweight removal procedure with the 3895 only — the 4095, 4595 and 1095 do it differently — and unlike the Hi-Point pistols the carbine has NO magazine disconnect, so it will fire with the magazine out. The yellow chamber plug that came in the box is used during the strip, not just for storage.

steps.title: Magazine out — this carbine has NO magazine disconnect
steps.action: Press the magazine release behind the trigger guard on the left of the grip and pull the magazine out. Then discard the habit you may have from Hi-Point's pistols: the carbines have no magazine disconnect and no magazine lockout, so removing the magazine does nothing whatever to the trigger. A chambered round will still fire with the magazine on the bench.
steps.prose: Standard magazine capacity for the 995 is ten rounds.
steps.caution: Two figures on this same page are model-specific and are the 995's, not the line's: "• 16-1/2” Barrel- 995/3895 • 17-5/8” Barrel- 4095/4595/1095", and "• Last Round Hold Open • 10 Rounds Magazine Capacity 9 Rounds 4595" — so a 995 is the short-barrel, ten-round member of the family and the nine-round figure belongs to the 4595 alone.
steps.quote: Hi-Point carbines do not have a magazine disconnect safety and can still be fired with the magazine removed.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL 3895 .380 ACP / MODEL 995 9MM / MODEL 4095 .40 S&W / MODEL 4595 .45 ACP / MODEL 1095 10MM AUTO — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 1, Frame with Integrated Barrel, p.8
steps.warn: Your Hi-Point carbine does not have a magazine disconnect and will still fire with the magazine removed.

steps.title: Thumb safety down, charging handle fully back, lock the bolt open
steps.action: Push the thumb safety fully down to the off (fire) position — the breech bolt cannot be removed with it up. Grip the stock with one hand, finger off the trigger, and pull the operating handle fully rearward to eject anything chambered. Lock the bolt open by pushing the operating handle roller into the round opening in the receiver shroud slot until it catches there; that round hole is the carbine's hold-open notch.
steps.prose: Then look into the chamber and the magazine well and check both with a fingertip — the last round hold open is not the check.
steps.caution: Always wear safety glasses when disassembling your Hi-Point carbine, to protect your eyes from components that are under pressure, such as springs, and the sear assembly that could fly out and hit you.
steps.quote: 4. Lock the breech bolt in the rearward (open) position by pushing the operating/charging handle roller into the round opening in the receiver shroud slot until it locks in the open position. (FIG. 4)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL 3895 .380 ACP / MODEL 995 9MM / MODEL 4095 .40 S&W / MODEL 4595 .45 ACP / MODEL 1095 10MM AUTO — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 9, Disassembly, step 4, p.26

steps.title: Yellow chamber plug in, then drop the striker
steps.action: Once you are satisfied the carbine is empty, release the breech bolt and put the yellow safety plug into the chamber — that is what it is for, and it is what makes the next action safe to perform. With the carbine pointed in a safe direction, pull the trigger to release the striker. You can strip the gun with the striker cocked but the bolt fights you; released, it comes off far more easily.
steps.prose: If you do not have a chamber plug Hi-Point will send one free; it is used again at the end of reassembly.
steps.quote: Once you are sure your Hi-Point carbine is unloaded, release the breech bolt and place the yellow safety plug into the chamber. (FIG. 5.1) Next, with your Hi-Point carbine pointed in a safe direction (a safe direction is one in which no one can possibly be injured in the event on an unintentional discharge) pull the trigger to release the striker.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL 3895 .380 ACP / MODEL 995 9MM / MODEL 4095 .40 S&W / MODEL 4595 .45 ACP / MODEL 1095 10MM AUTO — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 9, Disassembly, step 5, p.26

steps.title: Unscrew the operating handle out of the breech bolt
steps.action: Take the Hi-Point adjusting tool that came with the carbine and unscrew the operating/charging handle out of the side of the breech bolt. It is a threaded part, not a captive one, and it must come off before the shroud will lift. Then roll the rail lock back with the same tool to unlock the forend cover, push the cover forward and lift it away.
steps.prose: Keep the handle and its roller together; they go back in through the left-side slot in the shroud.
steps.quote: 6. Using the Hi-Point adjusting tool, remove the operating/charging handle by unscrewing it from the breech bolt. (FIG. 6)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL 3895 .380 ACP / MODEL 995 9MM / MODEL 4095 .40 S&W / MODEL 4595 .45 ACP / MODEL 1095 10MM AUTO — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 9, Disassembly, step 6, p.26

steps.title: Shroud clips clockwise, shroud pins out, receiver shroud off
steps.action: Press the shroud pins in from the head side and, while they are depressed, rotate the shroud clips clockwise with the adjusting tool to unlock them. Then push the shroud pins out of the receiver shroud with the screwdriver end of the tool or a punch. Lift the front of the receiver shroud and pull it off. The pins are spring-loaded, which is why they have to be held in while the clips turn — let them out and the clips will not index.
steps.prose: The shroud carries the rear sight assembly, so set it somewhere it will not get leaned on.
steps.quote: 7. While depressing the shroud pins from the head side, rotate the shroud clips clockwise with the Hi-Point adjusting tool to unlock them. (FIG. 7)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL 3895 .380 ACP / MODEL 995 9MM / MODEL 4095 .40 S&W / MODEL 4595 .45 ACP / MODEL 1095 10MM AUTO — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 9, Disassembly, step 7, p.27

steps.title: Receiver clip off the lug, firing assembly out of the stock
steps.action: Turn the carbine over and tap the receiver clip forward off the receiver lug on the underside, using the adjusting tool or a punch and a small hammer. With the clip gone, lift the front of the barrel and the whole firing assembly comes up out of the stock. The stock on a Hi-Point carbine is a shell — the receiver, barrel, trigger group and bolt all live in one assembly that sits inside it.
steps.prose: The clip is small and springs away when it releases; work over the bench, not over a carpet.
steps.quote: 11. Remove the firing assembly by lifting up on the front of the barrel. (FIG. 11)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL 3895 .380 ACP / MODEL 995 9MM / MODEL 4095 .40 S&W / MODEL 4595 .45 ACP / MODEL 1095 10MM AUTO — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 9, Disassembly, step 11, p.28

steps.title: Front sight off with a 5/64 hex, barrel frame support forward
steps.action: The breech bolt comes off over the muzzle, so anything on the muzzle has to go first. Loosen the two set screws on the bottom of the front sight base with a 5/64 inch hex key and lift the sight off, then slide the barrel frame support forward off the muzzle. Note where the sight was sitting on the rail — it goes back to the same place and then gets re-aligned by eye down the carbine.
steps.prose: Two set screws, not one; the sight will feel loose after the first and still be held.
steps.quote: 12. To completely remove the breech bolt from the firing assembly, you must first remove the front sight by loosening the 2 set screws on the bottom of the front sight base with a 5/64” hex key. (FIG. 12)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL 3895 .380 ACP / MODEL 995 9MM / MODEL 4095 .40 S&W / MODEL 4595 .45 ACP / MODEL 1095 10MM AUTO — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 9, Disassembly, step 12, p.28

steps.title: Retainer clip back, then bolt back 3/8 inch, up and forward
steps.action: Slide the breech bolt retainer clip back with the adjusting tool or a flat screwdriver to release the retainer. Now take the yellow chamber plug out, push the breech bolt back about three eighths of an inch to pull the firing pin clear of the barrel, and lift the back of the bolt up and over the barrel, sliding it toward the muzzle. Do that short rearward push first or you bend the striker against the barrel — the same trap as on the pistols.
steps.prose: The bolt is under main recoil spring tension at this point and the spring can jump out; keep a hand over it.
steps.quote: 15. At this point, the yellow safety plug may be removed. Push the breech bolt back approximately 3/8 inch to clear the firing pin/striker from the barrel and lift the back of the breech bolt up and over the barrel sliding it to the front of the carbine. (FIG. 15) Note: Use caution, the breech bolt is under spring tension from the main recoil spring and the main recoil spring may fly out.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL 3895 .380 ACP / MODEL 995 9MM / MODEL 4095 .40 S&W / MODEL 4595 .45 ACP / MODEL 1095 10MM AUTO — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 9, Disassembly, step 15, p.29
steps.warn: Main recoil spring under tension — eye protection, and keep a hand over it.

steps.title: Bolt off the muzzle, then the firing pin group out of it
steps.action: Slide the breech bolt the rest of the way off over the muzzle. It still contains the retainer, the firing pin/striker and their springs, so keep it the right way up until it is clear. Then pull the bolt retainer out of the rear of the bolt, turn the bolt upside down and let the firing pin spring, the firing pin assist spring and the striker slide out of the back. Finally draw the main recoil spring forward out of the frame.
steps.prose: That is the last of it; do not pull the trigger now, with the bolt off the sear is exposed and spring-loaded.
steps.quote: 17. Pull the bolt retainer out of the back of the breech bolt then turn the breech bolt upside down and allow the firing pin spring, firing pin assist spring and firing pin/striker to slide out the back. (FIG. 17)
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL 3895 .380 ACP / MODEL 995 9MM / MODEL 4095 .40 S&W / MODEL 4595 .45 ACP / MODEL 1095 10MM AUTO — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 9, Disassembly, step 17, p.29
steps.warn: Do not pull the trigger with breech bolt removed, the sear is under spring tension and could fly out.

steps.title: 995 counterweight — pivot pin rotates UP and out the receiver slot
steps.action: This is where the 995 parts company with half its own manual. On the 995 and the 3895, the counterweight and its pivot pin come out by rotating the pivot pin up to vertical and sliding it out through the SLOT IN THE RECEIVER; the counterweight then drops free of the frame on its own. The 4095, 4595 and 1095 do the opposite — theirs slide out through the TOP of the frame — so do not read that instruction and apply it here. Catch the counterweight; it is a drop-safety part and it falls the moment the pin is out.
steps.prose: It goes back in the reverse way: up through the magazine well, short end of the pivot pin in through the side slot, then the pin arm rotated down into its slot.
steps.caution: The 4095/4595/1095 procedure is different: "21. (For Models: 4095/4595/1095) Remove the counterweight and pivot pin by sliding then out through the top of the frame." That is not the 995's procedure. The REFIT branches the same way — for a 995 it is "4. (For Models: 995/3895) Install the counterweight up through the magazine well into the counterweight slot in the frame." (p.36), which is the reverse of what you have just done and not the route the larger-calibre carbines take.
steps.quote: 20. (For Models: 995/3895) Remove the counterweight and pivot pin by rotating the pivot pin up vertically and sliding it out through the slot in the receiver. (FIG. 20 & 20.1) Note: The counterweight will drop free from the frame when the pivot pin is removed.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL 3895 .380 ACP / MODEL 995 9MM / MODEL 4095 .40 S&W / MODEL 4595 .45 ACP / MODEL 1095 10MM AUTO — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 9, Disassembly, step 20, p.30

steps.title: Jacketed ammunition only in a 995
steps.action: Before it goes back together, know what it may be fed. Hi-Point restricts the carbines to jacketed ammunition to stop lead building up in the barrel, and this barrel is integral to a zinc-alloy frame rather than a part you can replace when it fouls badly. The 995 is rated for +P 9mm, so pressure is not the limit here — bullet construction is.
steps.prose: Only commercially manufactured ammunition meeting SAAMI, CIP or NATO standards.
steps.quote: Only use jacketed ammunition to prevent the buildup of lead deposits in the barrel.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL 3895 .380 ACP / MODEL 995 9MM / MODEL 4095 .40 S&W / MODEL 4595 .45 ACP / MODEL 1095 10MM AUTO — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 4, Loading, p.14
steps.warn: Use of improper ammunition could cause death or serious personal injury and/or property damage.

steps.title: Barrel from the chamber end, then the bolt face and extractor
steps.action: Run a solvent-wet patch through the barrel from the chamber end several times, then a solvent-wet brush back and forth from the same end, then an oiled patch, repeating until it comes out clean. Then brush the outside of the barrel — on this carbine the bolt rides on it. On the breech bolt, brush the bottom surfaces where it sits on the frame, then the breech face and under the extractor with the bolt held muzzle-end down so debris falls out rather than in.
steps.prose: Run clean dry patches through before firing so no oil is left in the bore.
steps.quote: 1. Wet a cleaning patch with a gun cleaning solvent or a cleaner-lubricantpreservative and run it through the barrel, from the chamber end, several times using a cleaning rod.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL 3895 .380 ACP / MODEL 995 9MM / MODEL 4095 .40 S&W / MODEL 4595 .45 ACP / MODEL 1095 10MM AUTO — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 10, Complete Cleaning, Barrel, p.31

steps.title: Powder-coated frame — no acetone, no Gun Scrubber
steps.action: The carbine's frame is powder coated, and that finish is chemically softer than the metal under it. Keep acetone, Gun Scrubber and other harsh solvents off it — they strip the coating and what is left is bare zinc alloy that corrodes. Wipe the frame with a patch only slightly dampened with a cleaner-lubricant-preservative, and if you want to use a product you have not used on this gun before, try it on a small area first.
steps.prose: The stock is a separate polymer shell and needs nothing but a wipe.
steps.quote: The frame has a powder coat finish. Do not use acetones, Gun Scrubber®, or harsh solvents that may remove the coating. Test new cleaning products on a small surface before using them.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL 3895 .380 ACP / MODEL 995 9MM / MODEL 4095 .40 S&W / MODEL 4595 .45 ACP / MODEL 1095 10MM AUTO — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 10, Complete Cleaning, p.33

steps.title: Interval — 1,500 to 2,000 rounds, lubricated sparingly
steps.action: Hi-Point's complete-clean interval for the carbine is every 1,500 to 2,000 rounds, or any time it gets wet or is exposed to weather. Afterwards, lightly oil the outside of the barrel, the inside of the breech bolt and the outside of the magazine and stop there. This is a blowback action carrying a heavy bolt and a stout recoil spring; too much oil collects unburned powder into a paste that slows the bolt and causes the short-stroking people blame on ammunition.
steps.prose: While it is apart, check the barrel for lead build-up, bulges or cracks, and check the magazine follower springs back freely.
steps.quote: You should completely clean your Hi-Point carbine after firing every 1,500 to 2,000 rounds or anytime it is exposed to the elements, becomes wet, etc.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL 3895 .380 ACP / MODEL 995 9MM / MODEL 4095 .40 S&W / MODEL 4595 .45 ACP / MODEL 1095 10MM AUTO — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 10, Complete Cleaning, p.31

steps.title: Retainer clip THROUGH the slot, not under it
steps.action: On reassembly the breech bolt retainer clip must lock through the slot in the retainer, not sit underneath it. Push it forward until it is genuinely through, and check by eye. This is the carbine's silent failure: it will still fire with the clip under the retainer, but the breech bolt is not properly locked in place, and an unretained bolt on a blowback carbine travels rearward under recoil with nothing to stop it.
steps.prose: The same class of check as the front sight set screws — verify it, do not assume the parts fell together correctly.
steps.quote: Make sure that the retainer clip is properly locked through the slot in the breech bolt retainer and not under it. Your Hi-Point carbine may still fire but the breech bolt will not be properly locked in place which could lead to serious personal injury, and/ or damage your Hi-Point carbine.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL 3895 .380 ACP / MODEL 995 9MM / MODEL 4095 .40 S&W / MODEL 4595 .45 ACP / MODEL 1095 10MM AUTO — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 11, Assembly, p.38
steps.warn: Clip through the slot. There is no other cue that the bolt is unretained.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Laid out: stock, receiver shroud with its rear sight, forend cover, front sight, barrel frame support, firing assembly with the barrel and frame, breech bolt, bolt retainer, striker with its two springs, main recoil spring, counterweight and pivot pin, sear and sear spring, operating handle, and the magazine. That is the whole of the 995TS strip Hi-Point publishes, and it says plainly that anything beyond it voids the warranty and can make the carbine malfunction.
steps.prose: Reassembly is the reverse, with the 995/3895 counterweight route, the retainer clip check, and the front sight re-aligned by sighting down the carbine before the set screws go tight.
steps.quote: Never disassemble your Hi-Point carbine further than this procedure. Any further disassembly by untrained persons could cause your Hi-Point carbine to malfunction and will void the warranty.
steps.cite: HI-POINT FIREARMS INSTRUCTION MANUAL — MODEL 3895 .380 ACP / MODEL 995 9MM / MODEL 4095 .40 S&W / MODEL 4595 .45 ACP / MODEL 1095 10MM AUTO — UNKNOWN — no version marker, part number or revision code is printed anywhere in this document — Chapter 9, Disassembly, p.30

deepAbsentReason: Hi-Point publishes no deeper teardown for the 995TS and forbids one: "Never disassemble your Hi-Point carbine further than this procedure. Any further disassembly by untrained persons could cause your Hi-Point carbine to malfunction and will void the warranty." (Chapter 9, Disassembly, p.30). The 21-step procedure walked above IS the manual's complete disassembly and it already goes well past a field strip — shroud, forend cover, front sight, firing assembly out of the stock, breech bolt off the barrel, striker and springs out of the bolt, main recoil spring, sear and sear spring, and the counterweight with its pivot pin. Everything the manual describes as removable has been walked, so there is no further procedure to author a deep branch from; a Deep Clean here would have to be invented.

cleaning.name: BARREL — FROM THE CHAMBER END
tasks: Solvent-wet patch through from the CHAMBER end, several times, with a cleaning rod
Solvent-wet bristled brush back and forth from the chamber end
Oiled patch through once and examined; repeat brush-and-patch until clean
Clean dry patches until no oil comes out — skip only if it is going into storage
Nylon brush and solvent over the OUTSIDE of the barrel, then wipe dry: the bolt rides on it

cleaning.name: BREECH BOLT
tasks: Nylon brush and solvent on the bottom surfaces where the bolt sits on the frame
Oil-wet nylon brush on the breech face and under the extractor, bolt held muzzle-end down
Wipe with clean patches until they come away clean
Check the remaining exposed bolt surfaces for debris

cleaning.name: FRAME — POWDER COATED
tasks: NO acetone, NO Gun Scrubber, no harsh solvents — they strip the powder coat
Test any unfamiliar cleaning product on a small area first
Wipe exposed frame parts with a patch slightly dampened with cleaner-lubricant-preservative

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE & LUBRICATION
tasks: Wipe the magazine body and feed lips with a slightly dampened patch
Press the follower down with a fingertip and release — it must spring back and not catch
Complete clean every 1,500-2,000 rounds, or any time the carbine gets wet
Lightly oiled patch on the outside of the barrel, the inside of the breech bolt and the outside of the magazine — that is all of it
Do not over-lubricate; excess collects unburned powder and slows the bolt
Inspect the barrel for lead build-up, bulges, cracks or obstructions before reassembly

reassembly: Roll the firing pin on a flat surface first and watch the end for wobble — a bent striker is replaced, not refitted.
Firing pin, then its spring and assist spring, down into the rear channel of the breech bolt, bolt held muzzle-down.
Slide retainer into the rear of the bolt, spring guide facing forward.

995/3895 ROUTE: counterweight up through the magazine well into its slot in the frame; with it pushed fully up, insert the SHORT end of the pivot pin through the side slot into the hole in the counterweight; rotate the pivot pin arm down into its slot in the frame.
Hold the sear cam up and push the trigger disconnect down so the cam goes under the disconnect arm; fit the sear and sear spring into the sear hole with the sear ramp facing FORWARD.
Sear cam over the sear arm, arm through the hole in the cam — correct when the ramp faces forward, the pivot pin is under the sear arm and the disconnect arm moves freely.
Main recoil spring and guide rod into the frame below the barrel, guide rod forward.
Breech bolt over the muzzle and back along the barrel, aligning its bottom tab with the end of the main spring guide, retracted far enough to clear a protruding firing pin.
Align the retainer with its hole in the frame, push the bolt down, then push the retainer clip FORWARD so it locks THROUGH the retainer slot — not under it.
Barrel frame support over the muzzle and back onto the front lug.
Firing assembly into the stock rear-first, front pushed down so the receiver lug protrudes underneath; receiver clip over the lug, small bend away from the stock, seated over the bump.

Receiver shroud on back-end first with its support plate inside the stock; shroud clips rotated clockwise, shroud pins pushed through, then the clips turned counterclockwise onto the pin slots while the pins are held compressed.
Forend cover over the barrel with the rail lock open, slid back under the top rail, then the rail lock rotated forward to lock it.
Front sight back over the muzzle into the rail slot; sight down the carbine to align it before tightening both 5/64 set screws.
Operating handle and roller screwed into the bolt through the left-side shroud slot and tightened firmly with the adjusting tool.
Yellow safety plug back into the chamber to prove the carbine is unloaded.
fncheck: With the carbine confirmed empty, run Hi-Point's function test. Insert an empty magazine and feel it lock in; with the safety down, pull the operating handle fully back and release it and confirm the internal breech bolt lock holds it open. Press the magazine release and check the magazine drops out easily, then leave it out. Cycle the bolt several times, finger off the trigger, to confirm it runs freely. Pull the handle fully back and push the roller into the round shroud opening to lock it manually, then pull the roller out and let the bolt run forward on its own. With the safety UP, the trigger must do nothing, both with and without an empty magazine in place; with the safety DOWN, the trigger must release the striker. Remember throughout that this carbine has no magazine disconnect — the muzzle direction is doing all the work.
